title: How the Go SDK encodes ZIA writes (omitted zero values, empty responses)

prose.text: These are claims about the Go SDK, the client, not about ZIA. The distinction matters: SDK code proves what the client sends and how it reacts; what ZIA does with that is server behavior that code alone cannot settle.

marshals-caller-struct.statement: ZIA updates go through an `updateGeneric`, the OneAPI client's in `ziarequests.go` or, when the legacy client is configured, its own copy in `zia/v2_client.go`. Both serialize the caller's struct directly with `json.Marshal`, so each field's JSON tag alone decides whether it is sent.

rule-bools-omitted-when-false.statement: The URL Filtering rule struct tags its boolean fields `omitempty` (`blockOverride`, `enforceTimeValidity`, `ciparule`), so a false value is never sent on create or update.
rule-bools-omitted-when-false.conditions: Chain of evidence: the fields are tagged omitempty, no custom marshaller exists on the rule type, and Go's encoding/json omits a false bool so tagged. Other rule structs are not yet checked.

settings-bools-fixed-3-8-45.statement: The advanced URL and cloud-app settings booleans were tagged `omitempty` through v3.8.44. From v3.8.45 they are always sent, except `blockSkype` (and the `safeSearchApps` list), because, in the SDK maintainers' words, dropping a false from the body would leave the setting enabled.

empty-body-nil-nil.statement: When an update returns an empty body (for example 204 No Content), `updateGeneric` returns a nil result and a nil error.

rule-omission-semantics.title: Whether ZIA rule updates treat an omitted field as unchanged or as reset
rule-omission-semantics.blocks: saying whether a boolean or numeric rule field can be cleared (set false or 0) through the Go SDK or Terraform
rule-omission-semantics.detail: If omission keeps the stored value, the omitted false means a rule field set true can never be cleared through the SDK. The 2026-08 provider audit inferred exactly that for every omitempty field in every provider; that inference is not verified for rule endpoints. The maintainers state the keep-value behavior only for the settings endpoint (claim settings-bools-fixed-3-8-45). Resolve with a scratch-tenant test: set a rule's blockOverride true, update with it false through the SDK, re-read.

rule-update-empty-body.title: Whether ZIA rule update endpoints ever return an empty body
rule-update-empty-body.blocks: saying whether the update panic happens in practice
rule-update-empty-body.detail: The panic is certain if the body is empty (claims empty-body-nil-nil and rule-update-panics-on-empty-body). Whether the URL Filtering rules endpoint ever answers an update that way is server behavior that code cannot show.
